summary: Computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning are the working deployments - the sector's AI mostly watches the jobsite and checks the model against reality before concrete is poured.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, construction firms are asked directly whether they used AI in the last two weeks, and the latest reading is 16.0%, up from 14.3% in the prior period. The series was first asked in September 2023, so this is a measured adoption figure rather than an estimate.

BuiltWorlds runs the sector intelligence for construction technology and holds an annual AI/ML Conference covering artificial intelligence and machine learning across the architecture, engineering, construction, and operations industry. Its material points to use cases across the construction, building, and operation process, with implementation discussed at both project and enterprise levels. The page coverage sourced from BuiltWorlds and AGC highlights computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning as areas of focus. BuiltWorlds also tracks site robotics, jobsite IoT, and digital preconstruction through its research programs.

AGC tracks contractor adoption and safety-technology compliance across US builders. Its excerpt does not give an AI adoption percentage, but it reports that construction input costs climbed 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, that war and tariff impacts are disrupting projects, and that contractors added 22,000 jobs in August while the construction unemployment rate hit 3.1%. These figures describe the operating environment rather than AI use specifically.

On vendors and money, CREtech and MetaProp track venture flow across architecture, engineering, and construction technology alongside property tech, but the excerpts provide no dollar amounts. BuiltWorlds describes itself as a membership network for buildings and infrastructure professionals and its AI/ML Conference includes a founders showcase on practical AI in construction, indicating vendor activity without quantifying investment.

The sources are silent on ROI evidence and on regulatory posture. BuiltWorlds promises case studies and lessons learned from specific solutions, but no quantified returns appear in the excerpts. A reader deciding whether to deploy should note that measured adoption is still a minority of construction firms at 16.0%, that the documented use cases concentrate in safety monitoring, clash detection, and site scanning, and that the available material offers case studies and tracking networks rather than hard ROI or regulatory guidance.

https://www.agc.org/.brief: The Associated General Contractors of America describes a leadership course for project executives and a connected platform for heavy civil and infrastructure work. The group says it has over 27,000 member firms and provides services to address member needs and protect the public interest. According to an association survey, construction input costs rose 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, with war and tariff impacts disrupting projects. The association also reports contractors added 22,000 jobs in August and the construction unemployment rate hit a record low of 3.1%, while firms struggle to fill openings.

https://builtworlds.com/.brief: BuiltWorlds operates a membership network for buildings and infrastructure professionals. The organization hosts an annual Buildings Conference addressing innovation in building development, design, materials and systems, with particular focus on data centers and AI infrastructure. It also runs an annual AI/ML Conference exploring artificial intelligence and machine learning adoption across the architecture, engineering, construction and operations industry, covering implementation strategies, use cases, and lessons learned from companies deploying these technologies.
